## How to read this report

- **Status.** SOURCED: the value is in the cited text. SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED: the source names the item but gives no usable value. UNKNOWN: no source at all. Unsourced records carry no value and an SME question.
- **Evidence.** A quote is verbatim text from the cited page, checked by test against a snapshot of that page. A figure transcription is what a figure drawing shows, read from the committed render (the figure labels have no text layer).
- **Cited only.** Kept for the record and never applied; the record named in 'overlaps' applies instead.
- **Strength** is the MUTCD heading: Standard, Guidance, Option, Support. Sect. 6P.01 para 02: figure content other than the notes is generally Guidance.

| --- | --- |
| Scope | Rules come from the MUTCD only. The Colorado, E Second St and Granite drafts are comparison material, not rule sources. The client, jurisdiction and deviation layers stay in the schema, empty. |
| Approval | All sourced values are usable for now. An SME approval step comes in a later slice. Nothing is approved by default; unsourced values stay SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED or UNKNOWN. |
| Q-A, figures | Values read only from a figure drawing are FIGURE_TRANSCRIPTION evidence tied to a committed render. TA-33's 500 ft and 100 ft (optional) stay SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED. |
| Q-B, Sect. 6N.11 | Encoded exactly as the source. The undivided four-lane reading stays a proposed interpretation (SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED); an undivided TA-33 site routes to an SME question. Divided roads match as encoded. |
| Q-C, shoulder taper | Both values stored as printed. Table 6B-3 '0.33 L' computes; Sect. 6B.08 para 10 'approximately 1/3 L' is cited Guidance. |
| Shifting taper | Table 6B-3 '0.5 L' computes; Sect. 6B.08 para 08 'approximately 1/2 L' is cited Guidance. |
| Sect. 6B.04 paras 03-06 | Loaded as Guidance, cited only, each marked as overlapping Table 6B-1 so nothing is applied twice. |
| Extra sourced values | Approximately 20 ft device spacing in one-lane two-way and downstream tapers (6B.08 paras 12, 14), the 6K.01 para 05 2 x speed extension and the 6N.08 15 ft median rule are loaded. |
| TA-10 road form | 'Not multi-lane' is encoded as lanes_per_direction < 2 from Sect. 6N.11 para 02 (see the reasoning below; the SME may overrule). |
| W16-2P | Optional on both TA-10 approaches (owner checked the 6P-10 render; the figure labels it '(optional)' on one approach only). |
| TA-6 | Stays UNDETERMINED until the low-speed cutoff and 'minor road' have sources. |
| Note-only signs | ROAD NARROWS, SHOULDER WORK and BE PREPARED TO STOP have no device records; they stay as note actions. |
| TA-33 'stationary' | The word 'Stationary' in the TA-33 title is not encoded as a condition (it would make duration a required fact). |
| Registry | The four new registry fields and the duration split are kept; the differences from plan section 4B are listed below as proposals. |
| schema_version | Carried by rule_pack/pack.json and every part file; rows inherit it (also recorded in CLAUDE.md). |
| RI double fines (history) | Before the scope change the owner placed RI double fines in the jurisdiction layer (plan section 10 called it a jurisdiction module; the slice spec and D-51 listed it under the client layer). The scope change then removed it from v1. |

| R-6P01-FIGURES-ARE-GUIDANCE | (text rule) | "In general, the procedures illustrated represent minimum solutions for the situations depicted. Except for the notes (which are clearly classified using headings as being Standard, Guidance, Option, or Support), the information presented in the typical applications can generally be regarded as Guidance." | Sect. 6P.01, para 02, p. 857 (Support) |
| R-6P01-MAY-DEVIATE | (text rule) | "TTC plans may deviate from the typical applications described in this Chapter to allow for conditions and requirements of a particular site or jurisdiction." | Sect. 6P.01, para 03, p. 857 (Option) |
| R-6P01-DEVICES-ADJUSTABLE | (text rule) | "Other devices may be added to supplement the devices and device spacing may be adjusted to provide additional reaction time or delineation. Fewer devices may be used based on field conditions." | Sect. 6P.01, para 04, p. 857 (Option) |

| R-6G10-P01-PEDESTRIAN-DETOUR-SIGNS | when pedestrian_detour_required EQ True; -> M4-9A_OR_M4-9B_FOR_PEDESTRIAN_REROUTE | "Bicyclist/ Pedestrian Detour (M4-9a) signs or Pedestrian Detour (M4-9b) signs should be used where pedestrian flow is rerouted (see Section 6I.02)." | Sect. 6G.10, para 01, p. 797 (Guidance) |
| R-6G10-P02-R9-9 | when addon_sidewalk_closed EQ True; -> R9-9_AT_START_AND_PRECEDING_INTERSECTIONS | "The SIDEWALK CLOSED (R9-9) sign should be installed at the beginning of the closed sidewalk, at the intersections preceding the closed sidewalk, and elsewhere along the closed sidewalk as needed." | Sect. 6G.10, para 02, p. 797 (Guidance) |

| R-6G10-P05-R9-11A | when addon_sidewalk_closed EQ True; -> R9-11A_BEYOND_REDIRECT_POINT | "The SIDEWALK CLOSED, (ARROW) CROSS HERE (R9-11a) sign should be installed just beyond the point to which pedestrians are being redirected." | Sect. 6G.10, para 05, p. 797 (Guidance) |

| R-6I02-P07-M4-9-STREET-NAME | when vehicle_detour_required EQ True; -> M4-9_WITH_STREET_NAME | "A Street Name sign should be placed above, or the street name should be incorporated into, a DETOUR (M4-9) sign to indicate the name of the street being detoured." | Sect. 6I.02, para 07, p. 812 (Guidance) |

| R-6I02-P11-M4-9A-ARROW | when pedestrian_detour_required EQ True; -> M4-9A_ARROW_REQUIRED | "If used, the Pedestrian/Bicyclist Detour sign shall have an arrow pointing in the appropriate direction." | Sect. 6I.02, para 11, p. 812 (Standard) |
| R-6I02-P12-M4-9A-ARROW-PLAQUE | when pedestrian_detour_required EQ True | "The arrow on a Pedestrian/Bicyclist Detour sign may be on the sign face or on a supplemental plaque." | Sect. 6I.02, para 12, p. 812 (Option) |
| R-6I02-P13-M4-9B-M4-9C | when pedestrian_detour_required EQ True; -> M4-9B_OR_M4-9C_SINGLE_MODE_DETOUR | "The Pedestrian Detour (M4-9b) sign or Bicyclist Detour (M4-9c) sign (see Figure 6I-1) may be used where a pedestrian or a bicyclist detour route (not both) has been established because of the closing of the pedestrian or bicycle facility to through traffic." | Sect. 6I.02, para 13, p. 812 (Option) |

| R-TA10-N6 | when curve_or_crest_near_zone EQ True; -> EXTEND_BUFFER_BEFORE_CURVE | "The buffer space should be extended so that the two-way traffic taper is placed before a horizontal (or crest vertical) curve to provide adequate sight distance for the flagger and a queue of stopped vehicles." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 6, p. 878 (Guidance) |
| R-TA10-N7 | when night_work EQ True; -> ILLUMINATE_FLAGGER_STATIONS | "At night, flagger stations shall be illuminated, except in emergencies." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 7, p. 878 (Standard) |
| R-TA10-N8 | (text rule) | "When used, the BE PREPARED TO STOP sign should be located between the Flagger sign and the ONE LANE ROAD sign." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 8, p. 878 (Guidance) |
| R-TA10-N9 | when grade_crossing_present EQ True; -> EXTEND_ZONE_BEFORE_GRADE_CROSSING | "When a grade crossing exists within or upstream of the transition area and it is anticipated that queues resulting from the lane closure might extend through the grade crossing, the TTC zone should be extended so that the transition area precedes the grade crossing." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 9, p. 878 (Guidance) |
| R-TA10-N10 | when grade_crossing_present EQ True | "When a grade crossing equipped with active warning devices exists within the activity area, provisions should be made for keeping flaggers informed as to the activation status of these warning devices." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 10, p. 878 (Guidance) |
| R-TA10-N11 | when grade_crossing_present EQ True | "When a grade crossing exists within the activity area, drivers operating on the left-hand side of the normal center line should be provided with comparable warning devices as for drivers operating on the right-hand side of the normal center line." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 11, p. 878 (Guidance) |
| R-TA10-N12 | when grade_crossing_present EQ True | "Early coordination with the railroad company or transit agency should occur before work starts." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 12, p. 878 (Guidance) |
| R-TA10-N13 | 15 ft; when grade_crossing_present EQ True | "A flagger or a uniformed law enforcement officer may be used at the grade crossing to minimize the probability that vehicles are stopped within 15 feet of the grade crossing, measured from both sides of the outside rails." | Sect. 6P.01, Fig. 6P-10, note 13, p. 878 (Option) |

**TA-10 'not multi-lane' (E-TA10-NOT-MULTI-LANE).** TA-10 is a two-lane road with one lane each way. The pack encodes this as `lanes_per_direction < 2`. The number 2 comes from Sect. 6N.11 para 02, which defines a multi-lane highway as one with "two or more lanes of moving motor vehicle traffic in one direction"; a road that is not multi-lane therefore has fewer than two lanes in each direction. With `oneway = false` (two-way traffic alternating through one lane, figure title) and `divided_highway = false` (Sect. 6N.09, two-lane highway), this matches the figure. It is treated as a literal reading of para 02, not an interpretation. If the SME disagrees, the condition becomes SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED and every TA-10 site goes to an SME question.

## Proposed amendment to D-60 (Sect. 6N.11)

Current D-60 text: "TA-33 is one OR'd rule covering divided roads and undivided roads with two or more lanes each way (6N.11)."

Source, Sect. 6N.11 para 06, p. 847 (Option): "When the right-hand lane is closed, TTC similar to that shown in Figure 6P-33 may be used for undivided or divided four-lane roads."

Proposed D-60 text: "TA-33 is one OR'd rule: (a) a divided highway with two or more lanes in the closed direction (figure title; 6N.11 paras 02 and 03), or (b) an undivided four-lane road with the right-hand lane closed (6N.11 para 06). Branch (b) is a proposed reading of 'four-lane' (two lanes each way) and stays SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED until the SME confirms it; until then an undivided site goes to an SME question. A left-lane (median-side) closure on an undivided road, or an undivided road with more than two lanes each way, is not covered by 6N.11 para 06."

Not edited in the plan; for the owner to decide.

**Superseded (S4b).** Owner decision D-91 (2026-10-30) and S4b stage E source branch (b) for the four-lane, right-lane case; broader undivided cases stay SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED. See 'S4b changes'.

## Proposals for the owner (not edited)

**D-51 (client practice layer, Proposed).** Proposal: mark D-51 as withdrawn for the MVP. The owner's S4 scope change makes the drafts comparison material only. The client layer stays in the schema, empty. If it is revived, each entry must cite its drawing and wait for SME confirmation, as D-51 already says.

**D-68 (traffic control method).** No change to the decision. The pack encodes it as R-TA10-METHOD-FLAGGER: code sets FLAGGER when TA-10 is chosen. Proposal: add to D-68 that the police variant has no rule-pack source in v1. The drafts print POLICE OFFICER AHEAD as 'W20-8' (open question 13); the SME review action that switches to police needs its own source or stays an SME exception.

**Open question 15 (who holds the approver role).** Proposal: keep the default (a configured list of approver users) and add that approvals are recorded outside the pack as {record id, pack hash, approver, time}. The pack itself stays DRAFT, so changing a value changes the hash and voids its approvals.

**Open question 17 (RIDOT and MassDOT documents).** The default 'MUTCD plus client layer' no longer holds. Proposal: change the default to 'MUTCD only'. The jurisdiction layer stays empty until a state document is supplied; RI double fines (Sect. 6G.08) come back only from such a document.

**Open question 18 (section 4B complete).** Proposal: the SME reviews the registry differences listed above together with this question.

**S8 client modules.** S8 lists add-on modules (no parking, side streets, pedestrian or sidewalk, RI double fines, police detail, arrow board) and 'buffers from the client layer or Table 6B-2'. Proposal: keep only what the MUTCD sources: side roads (TA-33 note 2, Standard, R-TA33-N2), arrow board (TA-33 note 7, R-TA33-N7; optional elsewhere) and buffers from Table 6B-2 (R-6B06-BUFFER-OPTION). Drop no parking, RI double fines and police detail from S8, or make them SME-added items. A pedestrian module needs Sect. 6G.10 loaded first (cited in the plan, not in v1). Also amend S8's acceptance: golden comparisons will differ where the drafts follow client practice (Colorado's 100 ft buffer against 155 ft from Table 6B-2, POLICE OFFICER AHEAD), so the S13 comparator should list these as known differences.
